scenes.title: Arrival at Pylos
scenes.summary: At sunrise the ship reaches Pylos, the citadel of Neleus, where the people are sacrificing black bulls to Poseidon on the shore, nine companies of five hundred men with nine bulls each; the crew puts in, and Telemachus steps ashore behind Athena.

scenes.title: Athena Encourages Telemachus
scenes.summary: Athena, in the likeness of Mentor, tells Telemachus that he has no more need of shame and must go straight to Nestor and question him. He is afraid he is too young and unpracticed in speech; she answers that he will think of some things himself, and a god will suggest the rest.

scenes.title: Peisistratus Welcomes the Strangers
scenes.summary: Nestor's son Peisistratus seats the strangers at the feast beside his father and his brother Thrasymedes and gives the golden cup first to Athena, as the elder. She prays to Poseidon for glory for Nestor and his sons, a gracious recompense for the Pylians' hecatomb, and a safe homecoming for Telemachus and herself, and brings it all to pass.

scenes.title: Telemachus Asks Nestor about His Father
scenes.summary: When they have eaten, Nestor asks the strangers who they are and whether they travel on business or roam like pirates. Telemachus, given daring by Athena, says that they come from Ithaca on a private errand, and begs Nestor to tell him plainly whatever he has seen or heard of his father's death.

scenes.title: The Sorrows at Troy
scenes.summary: Nestor recalls the sufferings of the war: there lie Ajax, Achilles, Patroclus and his own son Antilochus. No one could rival Odysseus in cunning, and Telemachus speaks so like him that Nestor marvels; Nestor and Odysseus never spoke at odds in assembly or council.

scenes.title: The Quarrel of the Sons of Atreus
scenes.summary: After the sack of Troy Athena's wrath sets the sons of Atreus at strife: in an assembly called at sunset, among men heavy with wine, Menelaus urges sailing and Agamemnon a sacrifice to appease the goddess. Half the army sails; at Tenedos a second quarrel sends Odysseus back to Agamemnon, while Nestor and Diomedes, joined by Menelaus at Lesbos, ask the god for a sign and cut across the open sea to Euboea, putting in at Geraestus by night; on the fourth day Diomedes' ships reach Argos, and Nestor sails on to Pylos.

scenes.title: The Returns of the Achaeans
scenes.summary: Nestor tells what he has heard: the Myrmidons came home safely, and Philoctetes, and Idomeneus without the loss of a man; Agamemnon came home to death at the hands of Aegisthus, and Orestes avenged him. He urges Telemachus to be valiant like Orestes, so that men to come may speak well of him.

scenes.title: Telemachus' Despair
scenes.summary: Telemachus wishes that the gods would give him the strength to punish the suitors. Nestor hopes that Athena may love him as openly as she loved Odysseus at Troy; Telemachus says it can never be, and Athena rebukes him: a god can easily save a man even from far away, but not even the gods can ward off death from a man they love.

scenes.title: Telemachus Asks about Agamemnon
scenes.summary: Telemachus gives up hope of his father's return and asks Nestor, who has reigned over three generations of men, how Agamemnon died, where Menelaus was, and how Aegisthus came to kill a far better man.

scenes.title: Aegisthus and Clytemnestra
scenes.summary: Had Menelaus found Aegisthus alive, he would have had no grave. While the Achaeans fought at Troy, Aegisthus sat at ease in Argos bewitching Clytemnestra with words; at first she refused, and a singer guarded her for Agamemnon, but when fate bound her he left the singer on a desert island for the birds, took her home willing, and burned thigh-pieces and hung up offerings to the gods for a deed beyond his hopes.

scenes.title: Menelaus' Wanderings and Orestes' Vengeance
scenes.summary: At Sunium Apollo killed Menelaus' helmsman Phrontis, and Menelaus stayed to bury him; off Malea a storm split his fleet, wrecking some ships on the rocks of Crete near Gortyn and carrying five to Egypt, where he gathered wealth among men of another tongue. Meanwhile Aegisthus ruled Mycenae for seven years, until in the eighth Orestes came back from Athens and killed him; on the very day of the funeral feast Menelaus arrived.

scenes.title: Nestor's Advice
scenes.summary: Nestor warns Telemachus not to stay long from home while the suitors devour his possessions, and urges him to go to Menelaus, who has lately come back from a sea so vast that not even birds come back from it within the year; he offers a chariot, horses and his sons as escorts to Lacedaemon.

scenes.title: Athena Takes Her Leave
scenes.summary: At sunset Athena bids them pour libations and go to rest. Nestor will not let Telemachus sleep on the ship as if he came from a poor man's house; Athena agrees that Telemachus should stay, says that she will go to the ship to hearten the crew and at dawn to the Caucones to collect a debt, and asks Nestor to send Telemachus on with a chariot and his son.

scenes.title: Nestor Knows the Goddess
scenes.summary: Athena departs in the likeness of a sea eagle, and all who see it are amazed. Nestor knows her for the daughter of Zeus, tells Telemachus that he will be no coward if the gods escort him so young, and vows Athena a yearling heifer with gilded horns; at home he mixes wine eleven years old and pours a libation to her.

scenes.title: Night in Nestor's House
scenes.summary: The guests go home; Telemachus sleeps on a corded bed in the colonnade beside Peisistratus, Nestor's unmarried son, and Nestor sleeps in the inner part of the house beside his wife.

scenes.title: Nestor's Orders at Dawn
scenes.summary: At dawn Nestor sits on the polished stones before his doors, where Neleus sat before him, with his six sons around him and Telemachus among them, and gives orders for the sacrifice to Athena: one son to fetch a heifer from the plain, one to bring Telemachus' crew, one to summon the goldsmith Laerces, and the rest to have the slave women prepare a feast.

scenes.title: The Sacrifice of the Heifer
scenes.summary: Laerces gilds the heifer's horns, and Athena comes to receive the sacrifice. Aretus brings water and barley grains, Perseus the bowl for the blood; Nestor begins the rite and prays, Thrasymedes strikes the heifer with the axe, the women raise the cry, and Peisistratus cuts her throat. The thigh-pieces are burned with wine, and the rest is roasted on spits.

scenes.title: Polycaste Bathes Telemachus
scenes.summary: Nestor's youngest daughter Polycaste bathes Telemachus and anoints him with oil, and he steps from the bath like the immortals in form and sits down beside Nestor for the feast.

scenes.title: The Drive toward Sparta
scenes.summary: Nestor has fine-maned horses yoked to a chariot for Telemachus, and the housekeeper stows bread, wine and food fit for kings. Telemachus and Peisistratus drive all day to Pherae, spend the night with Diocles, son of Ortilochus, and drive on at dawn across the wheat-bearing plain until the sun sets.

days.label: Day 3
days.note: Pylos: the sacrifice to Poseidon on the shore, Nestor's tales, Athena's departure, and the night in Nestor's house (3.1–403).

days.label: Day 4
days.note: The sacrifice to Athena, Telemachus' bath, the drive to Pherae and the night in Diocles' house (3.404–490).

days.label: Day 5
days.note: The drive across the wheat-bearing plain until sunset (3.491–497); the arrival at Lacedaemon follows (4.1).
